subject: Deliverable rights & training exemption — coordination and redline path
messages:
From: Emma Stone <emma@vertexa.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vertexa Legal <legal@vertexa.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Deliverable rights and training exclusion — initial redlines

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed the MSA + order form and came back with a request we need to land before procurement can sign: an explicit exclusion for customer deliverables and our uploaded dataset from any model training, fine-tuning, or internal research use by Redwood.

Attached is a PDF with proposed redlines (Vertexa_Redlines_11.30.pdf). The key ask is one paragraph to be added to the Order Form / Data Use section: “Customer Content and Deliverables are not to be used to train, improve, or otherwise update Redwood models or models operated by Redwood without prior written consent and executed DPA amendment.”

We understand that Redwood has a general feedback license and telemetry for product improvement. Our security team would accept a narrow carve-out: telemetry and anonymized usage metrics are fine, but no retention or downstream model training on raw customer-provided content or deliverables.

Can you confirm Redwood’s statutory position on this and share a proposed counter-language? If we can get alignment on wording, we can move to signatures this week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Victor Lin (IT) and I will be on standby for any legal back-and-forth.

Best,
Emma Stone
Head of Legal Ops
Vertexa, Inc.

Attachment: Vertexa_Redlines_11.30.pdf (pdf, 2 pages — redline markup)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Stone <emma@vertexa.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Deliverable rights and training exclusion — initial redlines

Emma — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the PDF. Good to meet Victor during the demo.

Short answer: Redwood is willing to discuss a limited carve-out for customer deliverables; we aim to protect customer content while preserving our ability to operate and improve the service. There are a few competing concerns (product telemetry, security/bug fixes, and an existing feedback license) we need to reconcile in precise contract language.

I've attached a proposed alternate clause (RWI-proposed-clause.txt) that tries to balance the asks:
- Explicitly excludes finalized customer deliverables and customer-uploaded datasets from training and model improvement activities without written opt-in.
- Preserves Redwood’s right to retain ephemeral telemetry, logs required for security/operational purposes, and aggregated usage metrics that do not contain customer content or PII.
- Offers an optional addendum path (Order Form checkbox) for customers who want to opt in to model improvement for a defined period and with compensation/discount (if Vertexa wants to pursue that later).

Laura (legal) — can you confirm whether the telemetry/bugfix carve-out language below is defensible from our compliance and product standpoint, and whether we should propose an explicit retention window for operational logs?

Emma — if that looks roughly aligned, can you loop in procurement and confirm the internal approver list? Happy to set a short call with Legal to finalize language today or tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 415-555-0123

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Deliverable rights and training exemption — coordination and redline path

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 9:12 AM Emma Stone <emma@vertexa.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed the MSA + order form and came back with a request we need to land before procurement can sign...

Emma / Sean — thank you for the context. I reviewed the Vertexa redlines and Redwood's proposed clause. Below are the legal points and a recommended compromise we can present to procurement: 

1) Customer Deliverables Exclusion (accept):
We can accept a carve-out: "Customer Deliverables" and "Customer-Uploaded Datasets" shall not be used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any Redwood models or third-party models operated by Redwood without the Customer's prior written consent.

2) Operational Logs & Security Exceptions (narrow carve-out, accept with retention limit):
Redwood must preserve the ability to retain ephemeral logs for security, abuse prevention, and to debug incidents. We propose a retention limit: operational logs retained up to 90 days unless required by law or active incident remediation. Logs used solely for security fixes shall be processed to remove substantive customer content where feasible.

3) Feedback License (restricted):
We can limit the existing feedback license to permit: aggregated, de-identified metrics and feature telemetry for product improvement. Any use of verbatim customer content for model training requires affirmative opt-in via the Order Form or a signed amendment.

4) Audit and Evidence (compromise):
To address Vertexa's audit needs, we will (a) provide a short attestation on our handling of Customer Deliverables, and (b) include an evidence checklist (logs/access list) available under NDA for a single audit per contract year.

5) Optional Commercial Path (opt-in):
If Vertexa is open to opting in to limited model improvement, we can offer a paid opt-in (term-limited), with the option for retraining credits or a discount. This keeps the core product improvements available for willing customers without exposing non-consenting customer content.

Action items: Sean / Priyom — propose the redline that implements 1–4 above. Emma — please confirm if procurement accepts a 90-day retention window for operational logs and if the audit attestation is sufficient. If so, we can generate clean MSA + Order Form language and circulate for signature.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference Legal — legal@redwoodinference.com

From: Emma Stone <emma@vertexa.com>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Deliverable rights & training exemption — coordination and redline path

Sean / Laura — thanks for the quick read and the thoughtful compromise. Vertexa accepts the proposed approach with two confirmations:

1) 90-day retention for operational logs is acceptable provided Redwood documents the categories of logs retained and provides the attestation annually.
2) The feedback license must explicitly note that aggregated telemetry does not include Customer Deliverables or verbatim customer content.

Procurement is ready to proceed to signature once we see the clean MSA + Order Form redline. Please send the updated documents and a DocuSign path. I have copied Victor for procurement ops.

Next steps per our calendar:
- Redwood to send clean redline (MSA + Order Form) by EOD 12/01
- Vertexa to sign via DocuSign once legal counters are incorporated
- Post-sign: onboarding kickoff (week of 12/6), procurement will route internal PO in parallel

Thanks again — excited to move forward.

Best,
Emma Stone
Head of Legal Ops
Vertexa, Inc.
